blockers.summary: apply_transaction only recognized lowercase injected_failure_stage values 'pre_mutation'/'post_mutation'. Any other truthy string fell through both known-stage branches, reached the real mutating _write_payload, then hit record_attempt's synthetic-SUCCEEDED guard which correctly raised PortableReleaseTransactionError -- but the wrapper's `except PortableReleaseTransactionError: raise` re-raised WITHOUT restoring, leaving torn state: disk mutated to the attempted payload while lineage.json still claimed the old generation/digest.
blockers.root_cause: Missing input validation before mutation (no whitelist/rejection of unrecognized injected_failure_stage strings) combined with a bare re-raise in the exception handler that assumed 'exception raised' always implied 'no mutation happened', which was false for this fall-through case.
blockers.repro_before_fix: INSTALL v1 (digest 6f6eb498c37dffb0) then UPDATE v2 with injected_failure_stage='POST_MUTATION' (uppercase) raised PortableReleaseTransactionError but left disk at digest a7ee5880a092eba2 while lineage still reported gen 0 / 6f6eb498c37dffb0 -- disk and lineage disagreeing.
blockers.fix_summary: Two changes to src/frankenstein2/self_update_transaction.py: (1) KNOWN_INJECTED_FAILURE_STAGES whitelist + _normalize_injected_failure_stage(), called before any plan is built or mutation attempted -- unrecognized values raise SelfUpdateTransactionError pre-mutation; normalization is case-insensitive by deliberate design (documented in-module), so the coordinator's exact repro string 'POST_MUTATION' now normalizes to the known 'post_mutation' alias and completes a clean ROLLED_BACK receipt with no exception and no torn state at all -- a stronger fix than raise-then-recover for that specific string. (2) A `mutated` flag set immediately after the real write in both apply_transaction and apply_rollback (apply_rollback had the identical unguarded-fall-through defect class and was fixed alongside it as a proactively-disclosed corollary finding, not part of the original repro); on any exception after that point, _recover_from_unexpected_post_mutation_failure() restores the exact predecessor snapshot and verifies the restored digest equals the expected source/predecessor state_sha256 before re-raising. If restore itself fails, a distinct hard error names both digests instead of silently propagating the original exception.

blockers.root_cause: logs/run_gates.py's _measure() helper was written to capture only wall-time/CPU/RSS/disk deltas; identity fields were never threaded through to the per-record schema.
blockers.fix_summary: logs/run_gates.py rewritten: schema bumped to F2_WP1207_SELF_INTEGRATION_MEASUREMENT/v2; _measure() now takes operation/parent_state_sha256/planned_target_state_sha256/expected_rollback_target_state_sha256 (or explicit *_reason fallbacks where genuinely not applicable) and emits repo_head_sha/repo_dirty (from real `git rev-parse HEAD` / `git status --porcelain` against this repo), a new _classify_failure() taxonomy, and observed_state_sha256/observed_lineage_generation/observed_lineage_state_sha256 read fresh from the store immediately after each gate. A new _planned_digest_for_payload() helper genuinely computes what a payload WOULD hash to by materializing it into a throwaway scratch tempdir (never MANAGED_DIR, never touches lineage/CAS) and hashing with the same compute_state_digest used everywhere else -- used where a target digest is knowable in advance (all INSTALL/UPDATE gates); for gates where no target digest is knowable pre-mutation as a matter of the gate's own logic (rejected-before-mutation gates like P8 hostile-twin, or the pure-readback P7), null + an explicit reason string is used instead -- never fabricated.
